A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PerpetualWonder and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary material. All 13 pages of each version support comparison, including content moved between the main text and appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original scene-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons on 10 scenes, a 350-participant user study, and main-text and supplementary ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–2, qualitative comparisons, ablations, and supplementary runtime results.

M1.justification: The VPP representation, scene initialization, progressive multi-view optimization, losses, and closed-loop physics updates remain unchanged in Section 3 and the supplementary implementation descriptions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 10-scene collection covering cloth, rigid bodies, elastic objects, liquids, gases, and granular substances. The long-horizon interactions and supplementary test scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Wan2.2, GEN3C, WonderPlay, Tora, Wan2.6, DaS, and Veo3.1. The comparator membership in the qualitative comparisons also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The WorldScore metrics and 350-participant, 10-scene 2AFC study protocol move from Section 4 to Appendix D without substantive revision. Simulation windows, rendering settings, and supervision views are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the VPP and progressive-optimization ablations in Figures 6–7, isotropic-versus-anisotropic comparison in Figure S1, radius sensitivity analysis in Figure S2, and unseen-geometry failure case in Figure S3.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; relocating the user-study protocol adds no uncertainty information.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings are retained. PerpetualWonder's Table 1 scores remain 93.26, 80.41, and 66.98; Table 2 preference percentages and Table S2 runtime values are also identical.

T1.justification: The scene and VPP definitions and equations (1)–(4), including temporal opacity and simulation-consistency loss, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about closed-loop simulation, unified physical and visual representation, multi-view consistency, and long-horizon action-conditioned generation.

C2.justification: The explanations of accumulated errors and progressive optimization remain unchanged. The limitations concerning optimization overhead and incomplete unseen geometry move from Appendix G to H without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, material-dependent VPP configurations, Table S1 simulation parameters, Table S2 runtime breakdown, and project-access information are retained. The relocated metrics passage does not disclose new technical details.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 63 cited works and research positioning, including the relationship to WonderPlay. The changed WorldScore citation back-reference reflects relocation of the metrics passage.

P1.justification: v2 moves the detailed metrics passage into new Appendix D, renumbering the subsequent appendix sections. It adds an author-affiliation footnote and funding acknowledgments, with otherwise limited wording and paragraph edits.

P2.justification: Supplementary Figures S1–S3 move from the upper-left to the lower-right portion of the final page, and Tables S1–S2 are repositioned. Text reflows and printed page numbers disappear, while figure content, captions, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds affiliation and funding information and modestly reorganizes the presentation. Moving the metrics passage to Appendix D preserves its content, while the methods, evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations remain unchanged. These editorial adjustments produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
